turns.text_snippet: The 404 is gone (URL is correct now), but there's a new error. "Load failed" is WebKit's generic fetch-failure message. Let me hit the actual endpoint to see what the backend returns now.

HTTP 307 — the endpoint is defined as `@router.get("/")` so the real path is `/api/features/` (trailing slash), and FastAPI redirects `/api/features` → `/api/features/`. Let me check the redirect target.

The redirect points to the **internal Docker hostname** `http://backend:8000/...`, which the browser can't reach — so following the 307 fails with "Load failed". The root cause is the route is `@router.get("/")` (trailing slash) while the frontend requests `/api/features` (no slash). Let me check the convention other routers use.

Confirmed: tasks.py and spaces.py use `@router.get("")`/`@router.post("")` (no trailing slash) for collection roots. features.py uses `"/"`, which triggers the 307 redirect to the unreachable internal hostname. Let me fix the two root routes to match the convention.
Now let me check whether any backend tests rely on the trailing-slash path.

Tests POST to `/api/features/` (trailing slash); with `redirect_slashes` (default on) the TestClient will follow the 307 to `/api/features`, so they should still pass. Let me run the feature tests to confirm.
Only one test failed — the others followed the redirect fine. Let me look at the failing test.

This test uses raw `httpx.AsyncClient` which doesn't follow redirects, so it correctly catches the trailing-slash behavior. The convention-aligned fix is route=`""` (matching tasks.py/spaces.py); I'll update the tests that hardcode the trailing-slash root path. Let me update them.
There's also `test_features_e2e.py`. Let me fix all the `/api/features/?space_id=` occurrences too.
This comment documents the exact bug. Let me update the comment and the three GET calls in the e2e test.
Now let me run both feature test files.
All 27 pass. Let me scan the whole test suite for any remaining bare-root trailing-slash references I may have missed.
The remaining matches are docstrings/comments or `/{id}` subpaths. Let me check the router registration test — it may assert on the root route paths.
This test already uses the no-slash form — it'll now pass directly. Let me run the full feature-related test set to confirm everything is green.
All 41 pass. Let me commit, then fast-forward to main and upgrade.
Both `main` and the task branch are updated. Let me record the pitfall in memory, then upgrade.

Both `origin/main` and the task branch now have the fix (commit `51b8fba`). Triggering the upgrade to deploy it.

**Root cause of "Load failed":** The features collection routes were declared `@router.get("/")`/`post("/")`, so the canonical path was `/api/features/`. A browser request to `/api/features` got a 307 redirect whose `Location` was the absolute internal Docker URL `http://backend:8000/api/features/...` — unreachable from the browser, surfacing as WebKit's "Load failed". I aligned the routes with the tasks/spaces convention (`@router.get("")`), updated the tests that hardcoded the trailing slash, and verified all 41 feature tests pass.

STATUS: DONE

The fix is in `origin/main` (`51b8fba`) and the upgrade has started.

Summary of this round:
- **Why it changed from 404 to "Load failed":** the first fix corrected the URL path, so the request finally reached the backend — which then 307-redirected `/api/features` to the unreachable internal hostname `http://backend:8000/...`.
- **Fix:** changed the two collection routes in `backend/app/api/features.py` from `@router.get("/")`/`post("/")` to the no-trailing-slash form (`""`), matching `tasks.py`/`spaces.py`. Updated the feature tests that hardcoded the slash; all 41 pass.
- Pushed to both main and the task branch, recorded the pitfall in memory, and triggered the upgrade. Once the container restart completes, the Features page should load.
